title: Review generic path: no case hard-coding + correctness

last_report.msg: approve-with-nits: no case literals in builder; borderline: success code '1'/returnCode envelope, fixed END_REASONS incl main_menu; risks: 15s timeout+1 retry on reads vs 12s mock, mutating detection by verb list, no Accept/Authorization headers, no waiting phrase guidance

spec:
Read-only review of orch/final vs main (git diff main...orch/final -- build-the-builder-v3/build-the-builder/builder build-the-builder-v3/build-the-builder/build.py) — tasks G, G2, X, P added a generic service-agent path to our agent BUILDER for the hackathon final case (folder "/Users/ulas/Desktop/Freya/Build the Builder - Final Case"). Hackathon rule: "do not hard-code this case into the builder"; the workflow is reviewed by judges and traces are read to check the agent came out of the builder.
Check within 15 minutes:
1. HARD-CODING: any case-specific literal in builder code (service/path names like cards.list, field names like customerNo/ibanEmail/debtTL, aiFlow/CardOps, Turkish sentences from the case, currency lists tied to the case, 'Freya Bank', customer numbers, file names of the case folder). Generic language support (Turkish number words/month names) is fine. List each with file:line and a generic alternative.
2. CORRECTNESS RISKS in the generic workflow for a live call: pre hook envelope building, post hook unwrap/errors, end nodes and transfer, variables {{customerNumber}}/{{now}}, timeouts (one mock answer takes 12 s), retries on mutating tools, prompt size (~5k tokens) — anything that would break calls.
3. Quick wins (≤10 min of coding each) ranked.
Verdict + ≤12 lines of concrete items (file:line, why, fix). Do not edit files.
